Looking at Example 1 (2024-08-12) - this is after a price decline from 72.65 to 70.14 over the last 18 days. The model is still forecasting mostly upward, averaging around 71.8x, but the true outcome continues to decline to ~62.82 by day 30.

Key observations:
- Model forecasts are too high relative to outcomes
- The decline in Example 1 is more pronounced than the model predicted
- Looking at Example 5 (2024-07-08) - similar pattern: model forecasts around 68.5-69.5, but outcomes go lower to 62.82

Let me look at Example 4 (2024-05-06):
- History shows prices from 62.85 upward to 74.25
- Model forecasts start at 73.09 but outcomes are higher at 73.67+
- Wait, looking more closely - the model seems to lag behind the true outcomes in this case

Let me re-examine Example 1 more carefully:
- Date: 2024-08-12
- History (last 18 days): starts at 70.14 and declines to 68.16 by day 9, then continues to 62.82 by day 30
- Model forecasts: start at 72.54 on day 1, gradually work their way down to 70.01 by day 30
- True outcomes: start at 72.65, decline to 62.82

The model is forecasting about 2-3 points too high on average. The decline in Example 1 is faster and further than the model predicted.

Example 2 (2024-08-09):
- Similar pattern - model forecasts ~2 points too high on average


- The divergence grows as prices continue to fall

Example 3 (2024-08-08):
- Model forecasts are approximately 1-2 points too high
- Outcomes consistently underperform model predictions

Example 5 (2024-07-08):
- Model forecasts begin 0.15-0.25 points too low
- Outcomes eventually fall more dramatically, diverging by 2-4 points
